# Draft:Recession indicators in popular culture

Recession indicators, in popular culture, are correlations involving cultural trends which are supposed indicators of impending economic recession. Such indicators have been said to involve trends in pop music, fashion, and consumer goods. These correlations have been criticized as spurious or unfounded.
Background
A recession is a contraction in the business cycle characterized by an overall decline in economic output and employment rate. Although the exact definition is disputed, Julius Shiskin's definition of "a decline in the seasonally and calendar adjusted real gross domestic product (GDP) in at least two successive quarters" is popular among business cycle analysts.
Origin
The idea of predicting recessions to cultural trends stretches back to the early 20th century. George Taylor of the Wharton School is frequently credited with the popularization of the hemline index, although contrary to popular belief, his work Significant post-war changes in the full-fashioned hosiery industry, although discussing skirt length, does not propose a correlation between skirt length and economic performance.
The phenomenon of cultural recession indicators gained renewed attention in 2025 amid economic uncertainty following tariff policies and trade tensions, with social media users on platforms like TikTok identifying various cultural shifts as tongue-in-cheek signs of impending economic downturn.
Supposed indicators
Fashion
A 2010 study by economists Marjolein van Baardwijk and Philip Hans Franses at the Erasmus School of Economics analyzed hemline data from 1921 to 2009, and found a statistically significant relationship between skirt lengths and stock market performance, in that hemlines tend to rise approximately three years before an economic upturn and fall three years before one.
Other fashion-related indicators include the high heel index (proposing that heel heights increase during recessions as consumers seek escapism) and observations about conservative or minimalist fashion trends during economic downturns. Following the 2008 recession, fashion shifted toward minimalism, with consumers focusing on timeless, simple designs rather than elaborate styles.
Music
Recession pop is a loosely defined style of music predominantly associated with dance-pop and electropop that emerged during the Great Recession in the United States in the late 2000s to early 2010s. The term describes upbeat, catchy, feel-good pop music characterized by fast tempos, high-energy rhythms, catchy melodies, and lyrics concerning hedonism, youthfulness, and partying, serving as both a critique of the era and a coping mechanism in the wake of economic hardship.
Food and groceries
Several consumer product trends have been identified as supposed recession indicators. For instance, sales of shelf-stable foods such as dried pasta, canned soups, and boxed macaroni and cheese have been observed to increase 4-6 months before economic downturns are officially announced. Other common grocery-related recession indicators include increased coupon usage and prominent canned goods displays at stores.
